title: Coding Shifts from Input to Output: Nadella Admits VS Code's Standing Was Rewritten Within Six Months

content_html:
Developers “not opening VS Code for months” has become a new talking point in the industry, and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella didn’t shy away from it. According to a Windows Latest report on November 23, he admitted that after Anthropic launched Claude Code, traditional code editors and IDEs lost their relevance in about six months—and Microsoft wasn’t able to come up with a response right away.

Ten years of work, lost in half a year

VS Code is the default developer workbench Microsoft spent more than a decade refining: free and open source, cross-platform, with syntax highlighting, intelligent completion, debugging, and Git integration all in one, while retaining users through its extension ecosystem. Nadella affirmed the team’s tradition of open development—product managers read community feedback every day and improve the product based on user opinions, so its success was no accident. But the change came from another direction: Anthropic made the model good enough, and also got developers to truly accept the command-line form, so writing programs shifted from “input” to “output.” When Cursor built a powerful agent mode on a VS Code fork, Microsoft could still catch up quickly; this time it was completely swept along by the pace. He drew a lesson from it: don’t become infatuated with what you’ve built.

Nadella also believes this is not a dead end. As Microsoft launches a new generation of decision models, IDEs may even see a renaissance—in the future, the core of the IDE will no longer be hand-coding programs, but “writing real Markdown documentation.” Adjustments are already underway: VS Code 1.146, released on November 11, added an agent inbox and model comparison features; a week later, 1.147 brought model routing, allowing users to choose from preferred models based on the task, and also supports scheduled agent requests and browser integration.
